subject.title: [Bug]: Cron isolated agentTurn skips delivery before dispatch when a recovered early tool error is classified as fatal

question: What cron outcome should OpenClaw record and deliver when an isolated agent session succeeds after a subprocess launched and exited nonzero?
rationale: The remaining behavior affects delivery, alerts, retries, and operator trust, and source evidence shows automation cannot safely choose between false success, false non-delivery, or degraded/warning semantics from current fields alone.

options.title: Design degraded cron outcome
options.body: Keep this issue open and implement typed exec phase evidence plus a first-class degraded/warning outcome before relaxing delivery policy.

options.title: Fail closed for launched failures
options.body: Keep delivery suppressed for launched nonzero process failures until maintainers define degraded delivery semantics.

options.title: Deliver recovered final output
options.body: Treat final assistant output after launched nonzero process failures as delivery-eligible, accepting that unresolved mutating failures may be hidden.

recommendation.title: Design degraded cron outcome
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and implement typed exec phase evidence plus a first-class degraded/warning outcome before relaxing delivery policy.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the current issue thread and authored the maintainer framing for the remaining decision.
